ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, $\angle B+\angle D=180^\circ$, $CE\perp AD$ at point $E$, $AE=10\,\text{cm}$, $AB=8\,\text{cm}$, what is the length of $DE$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, take $EF=DE$ on $AD$,\\
$\because CE\perp AD$,\\
$\therefore$ the line $CE$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment $FD$,\\
$\therefore CF=CD$,\\
$\therefore \angle D=\angle CFD$, $\angle AFC+\angle CFD=180^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B+\angle D=180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFC=\angle B$,\\
$\because \left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle B=\angle AFC \\
\angle BAC=\angle FAC \\
AC=AC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BAC\cong \triangle FAC$,\\
$\therefore AF=AB=8\text{cm}$, $EF=DE=AE-AF=AE-AB=10\text{cm}-8\text{cm}=2\text{cm}$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $DE=\boxed{2\text{cm}}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: A, E, D are collinear on the bottom line with E between A and D; C is above E and CE is drawn perpendicular to AD; B is above the quadrilateral and AC is the diagonal/angle-bisector from A. Use an auxiliary reflection construction. Choose point F on line AD on the A-side of E so that EF=DE. Since CE⊥AD and E is the midpoint of FD, CE is the perpendicular bisector of FD, so CF=CD. Hence triangle CFD is isosceles and ∠CFD=∠D. Because A,F,D are collinear, ∠AFC and ∠CFD are supplementary. Given from the text that ∠B+∠D=180°, conclude ∠AFC=∠B. Also, because AC bisects ∠BAD and F lies on AD, ∠FAC=∠BAC. With common side AC, triangles AFC and ABC are congruent, so AF=AB=8. From the figure/order, F lies between A and E after AF=8<AE=10, so EF=AE−AF=10−8=2. Since EF=DE, obtain DE=2 cm.

Put A=(0,0), AD on the x-axis, E=(10,0), C=(10,h), and D=(10+x,0), where x=DE. Let θ=∠CAD, so tanθ=h/10. Because AC bisects ∠BAD, ray AB makes angle 2θ with AD, and AB=8 gives B=(8cos2θ,8sin2θ), where cos2θ=(100−h^2)/(100+h^2) and sin2θ=20h/(100+h^2). The circle through A, C, D has equation X^2+Y^2−(10+x)X+((10x−h^2)/h)Y=0. Substitute the coordinates of B into this circle equation, using cyclicity. The simplification gives (x−2)(100+h^2)=0. 推理：因为图中四边形 ABCD 是凸四边形，且题设给出 ∠B+∠D=180°，所以 ABCD 为圆内接四边形。按指定坐标法，设 A=(0,0)，AD 在 x 轴上，E=(10,0)，C=(10,h)，D=(10+x,0)，其中 x=DE。设 θ=∠CAD，则 tanθ=h/10。因为 AC 平分 ∠BAD，所以 AB 与 AD 的夹角为 2θ；又 AB=8，所以 B=(8cos2θ,8sin2θ)。由倍角公式得 cos2θ=(100-h^2)/(100+h^2)，sin2θ=20h/(100+h^2)，因此 B=(8(100-h^2)/(100+h^2),160h/(100+h^2))。

推理：因为图中四边形 ABCD 是凸四边形，且题设给出 ∠B+∠D=180°，所以 ABCD 为圆内接四边形。按指定坐标法，设 A=(0,0)，AD 在 x 轴上，E=(10,0)，C=(10,h)，D=(10+x,0)，其中 x=DE。设 θ=∠CAD，则 tanθ=h/10。因为 AC 平分 ∠BAD，所以 AB 与 AD 的夹角为 2θ；又 AB=8，所以 B=(8cos2θ,8sin2θ)。由倍角公式得 cos2θ=(100-h^2)/(100+h^2)，sin2θ=20h/(100+h^2)，因此 B=(8(100-h^2)/(100+h^2),160h/(100+h^2))。

过 A、C、D 的圆方程可设为 X^2+Y^2-(10+x)X+((10x-h^2)/h)Y=0。由于 ABCD 共圆，点 B 也在此圆上。代入 B 的坐标：64-(10+x)·8(100-h^2)/(100+h^2)+((10x-h^2)/h)·160h/(100+h^2)=0。两边乘以 100+h^2 后化简得 8(x-2)(100+h^2)=0。因为 h>0，所以 100+h^2>0，故 x=2。于是 DE=x=2 cm。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route is analytic: it converts the diagram into coordinates and uses the cyclicity implied by opposite supplementary angles. It avoids the auxiliary point F and avoids proving triangle congruence synthetically.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the coordinate-friendly placement from the image: AD is the base line, E lies between A and D, CE is vertical/perpendicular to AD, C is above E, and the quadrilateral order makes ∠B and ∠D opposite angles.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use AC bisects ∠BAD, ∠B+∠D=180°, CE⊥AD, AE=10 cm, and AB=8 cm to set coordinates and angle relations.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the converse cyclic-quadrilateral theorem for opposite supplementary angles, double-angle formulas from tanθ=h/10, and the general equation of a circle through three points.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, $\angle B+\angle D=180^\circ$, $CE\perp AD$ at point $E$, $AE=10\,\text{cm}$, $AB=8\,\text{cm}$, what is the length of $DE$ in $\text{cm}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, take $EF=DE$ on $AD$,\\
$\because CE\perp AD$,\\
$\therefore$ the line $CE$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment $FD$,\\
$\therefore CF=CD$,\\
$\therefore \angle D=\angle CFD$, $\angle AFC+\angle CFD=180^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B+\angle D=180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFC=\angle B$,\\
$\because \left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle B=\angle AFC \\
\angle BAC=\angle FAC \\
AC=AC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BAC\cong \triangle FAC$,\\
$\therefore AF=AB=8\text{cm}$, $EF=DE=AE-AF=AE-AB=10\text{cm}-8\text{cm}=2\text{cm}$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $DE=\boxed{2\text{cm}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, E, and D are on the same bottom horizontal straight line, with E located between A and D; C is directly above E, CE is perpendicular to AD, and a right-angle symbol is marked at E; A and B, B and C, and C and D are all connected by line segments, and AC is the diagonal line from A to C. Reasoning: According to the auxiliary construction, take point F on straight line AD, on the side of E closer to A, so that EF=DE. Because CE⊥AD, and E is the midpoint of FD, CE is the perpendicular bisector of FD, therefore CF=CD. Thus triangle CFD is an isosceles triangle, ∠CFD=∠D. Also because A, F, and D are collinear, ∠AFC and ∠CFD are supplementary, that is, ∠AFC+∠CFD=180°. The given condition states ∠B+∠D=180°; combining with ∠CFD=∠D, it follows that ∠AFC=∠B. Also because AC bisects ∠BAD, and F lies on AD, ∠FAC=∠BAC. Together with the common side AC=AC, therefore △AFC and △ABC are congruent, so AF=AB=8 cm. It is known that AE=10 cm, and AF=8 cm<AE=10 cm, so F is between A and E, EF=AE−AF=10−8=2 cm. By the construction EF=DE, therefore DE=2 cm.
